mutations.because: A queued review has not started yet, but it will still post its findings once it does — counting only `in_progress` makes the wait treat it as already finished. The script then merges past a review that lands afterwards, which is exactly the race this lane exists to close. The test that plants a `queued` PR-Agent run with a single read expects the PR to be refused with the run named, and instead sees it merged.
command: a PR-Agent run still queued when the wait runs out refuses the PR and names the run

mutations.because: The name filter is what keeps the wait about PR-Agent and nothing else: without it, every unfinished run on the branch counts. A CI run still in progress on an older head of the same branch is waited for and then refuses a healthy pull request. The test that plants a completed PR-Agent pair beside an in-progress CI run expects the merge to go on without ever printing the waiting line, and instead the script refuses.
command: completed, skipped and other workflows' runs are not waited for
